data.title: Select
data.tagline: Choose one value from a collapsed list
data.description: Use a select when answers come from a fixed list but do not need to stay visible all the time. A few options are clearer as Radio buttons. If users may type their own answer, use an input or Autocomplete.

distinctions.label: Dropdown menu
distinctions.explanation: Select chooses a form value. Dropdown opens actions or navigation, such as Rename, Export, or Delete.

distinctions.label: Autocomplete
distinctions.explanation: Select chooses only from a fixed list. Autocomplete offers suggestions while someone types and may or may not permit a custom value.

use: A compact choice inside a form
avoid: Hide two or three simple choices in a dropdown
Use it when users need to compare long descriptions
Allow a value outside the list without making that clear
Leave the selected value ambiguous after the menu closes

lessonPractice.title: A form lets people choose one of four fixed, exclusive time zones. Which control fits?

options.label: Use a Select and show the current time zone
options.feedback: Correct. A selector saves space and clearly represents the current value for one option from a fixed set.

options.label: Use unrestricted text so people type a time zone
options.feedback: Free text easily creates invalid or inconsistent values.

options.label: Make the four peer values submit buttons
options.feedback: These are mutually exclusive values for one field, not four immediate actions.

data.agentPrompt: Change the time-zone field to a Select with fixed options, retaining the current value and clear names. Choose a new value by keyboard, save, then refresh and confirm display and stored value match.
